She wants lasting inquiry, recognition, delicious food, play, and company. These wishes make her more than a dispenser of harmful concoctions. Yet the same wish to continue can turn an objection into a new experiment, a symptom into usable information, or a material request into the next demand. The relationship question is therefore whether the other's answer can alter the encounter, including the purposes and costs of participation. Saya sometimes hears that answer, sometimes accommodates it, and sometimes evades its force.
